en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Part One: The Lion Section.
7. The Question on the Bat “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two qualities of the bat should be adopted,’ which are those two qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the bat enters a dwelling, moves about within it, and then departs, not becoming entangled there;”

In the same way, Great King, when a practitioner engaged in yoga has entered a village for alms and wandered from door to door, he should depart quickly with whatever he has obtained, and he should not become entangled there.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the bat that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, while living in another's house, the bat does not cause them any loss.
In the same way, Great King, when a practitioner of yoga has approached families,
he should not cause them any remorse— whether by excessive begging, by being overly insistent, by physical intrusions, by talking too much, or by sharing their joys and sorrows—
and he should not cause them to neglect their primary work; rather, he should desire only their prosperity in every respect.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the flying-fox that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* of the excellent *Dīgha Nikāya*:
“By purity in virtue, learning, and wisdom, ...”
By means of generosity, by righteous conduct, and by many good deeds—
with wealth, grain, fields, and lands,
with sons, wives, and quadrupeds.
He desires that his kinsmen, friends, and relatives,
as well as his strength, beauty, and happiness, should not both decline.
“And one desires the attainment of prosperity.
Thus ends the seventh question, the Vagguliṅga Question.
